## The call protocol

* Browser: `client::call(path, &args)` serializes `args` (a generated struct of the function's parameters by name) to JSON and `POST`s it with `content-type: application/json`, `accept: application/json`, `x-quench-rpc: 1`, and `Authorization: Bearer <access>` when `use_bearer` was called. Cookies are sent by the browser for same-origin requests.
* Server: the endpoint generated by `#[server]` runs `server::guard`, finds the user (if the function has `auth`), then `server::dispatch`: body (at most 1 MiB) read, JSON decoded into the argument struct, function run (inside `with_user` when it has `auth`), result serialized as JSON with status `200`.
* Errors travel as `ErrorBody` with the status of `ServerError::status()`.
* The path is `/_fn/<function name>` unless `#[server(path = "..")]`.

## Cross-site protection

The custom header is the primary CSRF defence for cookie sessions. A call without an `Authorization` header must in addition have `Sec-Fetch-Site` equal to `same-origin` or `none` when present, and an `Origin` whose authority equals `Host` when both are present. A request with neither `Sec-Fetch-Site` nor `Origin` passes these two checks.

## The HTML document

```html
<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>My app</title><link rel="stylesheet" href="/_quench/site.<hash>.css"></head>
<body><div id="app">...the view, as HTML...</div>
<script type="application/json" id="__q_state" nonce="N">{...}</script>
<script type="module" nonce="N" src="/_quench/quench.<hash>.js?wasm=/_quench/app.<hash>.wasm"></script>
</body></html>
```

The state script is present only when `Page::state` was called. Language, title, stylesheet `href` and `media`, and the two paths are HTML-escaped (`escape_attr`, `escape_text`). The view is rendered with `quench_ui::render_to_string`: reactive text shows its current value, listeners and effects are dropped, each dynamic or keyed region leaves an empty comment `<!---->`. With dev reload the tag `<script src="/_quench/dev.js"></script>` is inserted before the last `</body>` (appended if there is none). The golden file `tests/fixtures/page.html` (661 bytes, a single line without trailing newline) pins the whole document in `document_tests`.

## Escaping of state

`escape_json` replaces `<`, `>`, `&`, U+2028 and U+2029 by `\u` escapes. It does not validate the JSON.

## Assets

Name `app.wasm` with bytes hashing to `3f9a1c0b7d2e4a65` becomes `/_quench/app.3f9a1c0b7d2e4a65.wasm`. Replacement of an asset added under the same name removes the old entry by matching `/_quench/<stem>.<16 hex>.<ext>`, so `a.b.js` added as `a.b.js` is matched with stem `a.b`; a different asset whose name starts with the same stem plus a 16-hex-digit segment could theoretically collide. A request for an old hash is a 404, never a fallback to a page.

## Development reload

`/_quench/dev.js` is a one-line script (served `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, `cache-control: no-store`) that opens `EventSource('/_quench/dev')`; on error it closes the source and polls `fetch('/_quench/dev.js', {cache:'no-store'})` every 400 ms until it answers, then reloads. `/_quench/dev` is a server-sent events response (`cache-control: no-store`) that emits a `beat` comment every 15 seconds and never a message.

## Favicon

`/favicon.ico` answers `204` with `cache-control: public, max-age=86400` unless a page is registered at that exact path.

## Sessions on the server

`User` is built from claims. Order: `Claims` in extensions; bearer token (decoded with `JwtConfig::decode_claims`, audience check, live session check when a `SessionDb` is registered and the token has a `sid`); session cookie via `get_user_from_req`. Token validation allows 60 s of clock skew (stated in `testing::StubGatehouse::set_access_ttl`'s documentation; implemented in `quench-auth`).

## Client concurrency

`client` keeps a thread-local `State { bearer, on_unauthorized, generation, refreshing, failed }`. A call that gets 401 with a bearer set calls `renew(bearer, started_in)`. If the generation moved on since the call began, someone already refreshed and the call just retries. If a failure was recorded for that generation, it is returned. If a refresh is running, the call polls every 5 ms. Else it refreshes. One retry per call (`renewed`).

## wasm32

For `wasm32` the crate is `client`, `wire`, `error`, `user` and the macro re-export. `user()` always errors there. Server code is not compiled.
